title: Multimodal AI
teaser: Beyond text: images, voice and more

basics.say: Early chat assistants only handled text. Many models today are multimodal: they work with several kinds of input.
You can show one a photo of a whiteboard, a screenshot of an error or a chart, and ask questions about it.
You can talk to it and hear it answer. Some tools can also create images or fill in documents for you.
Behind the scenes it's the same idea: everything you give it is turned into tokens the model can work with.
Practical tip: when words fall short, add a picture. A screenshot often explains a problem faster than a paragraph.

deeper.say: Images are cut into small patches, a bit like tokens for pictures. Audio is cut into short slices of sound.
Seeing isn't understanding perfectly: models can misread small text, miscount objects or miss details in a busy image.
Creating images is often done by a specialized image model that the assistant calls behind the scenes.
Same rules as text: don't upload confidential documents or photos of client data into tools your company hasn't approved.

takeaway: Multimodal AI can read and create more than text: images, sound and documents.
